results.name: Arm Pulses Palms Upwards
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms bent at the elbows, with your forearms parallel to the floor and palms facing downwards.
Perform small, quick pulses by moving your forearms forward and backward, maintaining the position and height.
Continue pulsing in a controlled, rhythmic manner for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace and range of motion to ensure proper form.
results.description: Arm Pulses Palms Upwards is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arm Pulses
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your arms to make a 90-degree angle with the elbows while keeping your palms facing inward.
Tighten your upper arms and move your arms forward and backward in a pulse-like fashion.
Keep doing this activity for a suitable time.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements small and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on keeping your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
results.description: Arm Pulses is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arms Lateral Raise and Rotation Up
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, arms at your sides, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms laterally until they reach shoulder height while rotating your shoulders so your palms face upward (supinated).
Rotate your arms at the shoulder joint so that your palms face down.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your shoulders smoothly without forcing the range of motion.
Lift your arms under control and avoid using momentum.
Move only through a pain free range of motion.
Exhale as you raise your arms and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Arms Lateral Raise and Rotation Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Serratus Anterior, Upper Back.

results.name: Assault Airbike Fast Speed
instructions: Sit on the Assault AirBike's seat and adjust it to a comfortable height. Place your feet on the pedals and your hands on the handles.
Begin pedaling at a moderate pace. Simultaneously, push and pull the handles back and forth in a coordinated motion with your legs.
Gradually increase your pedaling speed and the intensity of your arm movements to achieve a fast pace.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a fast pace for the desired duration or number of intervals.
tips: Breathe steadily and maintain a consistent pace throughout the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
Perform the movement with control to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
results.description: Assault Airbike Fast Speed is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Assault Airbike Normal Speed
instructions: Sit on the seat of the Assault AirBike and adjust it to a comfortable height. Place your feet on the pedals and your hands on the handles.
Begin pedaling at a steady, moderate pace. Simultaneously, push and pull the handles back and forth in a coordinated motion with your legs.
Maintain a consistent speed and rhythm, ensuring smooth, controlled movements with both arms and legs.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a regular, steady pace for the desired duration or number of intervals.
tips: Breathe steadily and maintain a consistent pace throughout the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
Perform the movement with control to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
results.description: Assault Airbike Normal Speed is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Assault Airbike Sprint Speed
instructions: Sit on the Assault AirBike's seat and adjust it to a comfortable height. Place your feet on the pedals and your hands on the handles.
Begin pedaling at a moderate pace. Simultaneously, push and pull the handles back and forth in a coordinated motion with your legs.
Gradually increase your pedaling speed and the intensity of your arm movements to achieve a fast pace. Maintain a steady rhythm and ensure smooth, controlled movements.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles as fast as possible for the desired duration or number of intervals.
tips: Breathe steadily and maintain a consistent pace throughout the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
Perform the movement with control to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
results.description: Assault Airbike Sprint Speed is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Back Lever
instructions: Start by hanging on a bar with your arms extended overhead, hands placed shoulder-width apart, and your palms facing forward.
Pull yourself up until your head is facing the floor and your legs are overhead.
Pass your legs under the bar and align your body in a straight line from head to toe and parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for a suitable duration.
tips: Focus on engaging your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Ensure your grip on the bar is firm and secure to provide stability and prevent slipping.
Breathe steadily and evenly to help maintain the hold and reduce tension.
results.description: Back Lever is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Arms.

results.name: Ball Slams
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart while holding a medicine ball with both hands over your head.
Forcefully slam the ball straight into the ground, while pulling your hips back and bending your knees.
Retrieve the ball from the ground, return to the starting position and repeat with controlled, powerful repetitions.
tips: Engage your core before initiating each slam.Generate power from your hips and legs rather than using only your arms.
Keep your back neutral and avoid rounding your spine during the slam.
Perform each repetition with maximum power while maintaining proper technique.
Exhale forcefully during the slam and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Ball Slams is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Chest, Hamstrings.

results.name: Balloon Drill
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a balloon in front of you.
Toss the balloon into the air and tap it lightly to keep it afloat.
As the balloon is in the air, perform a squat by bending your knees and lowering your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Stand back up and tap the balloon again as it comes down, repeating the process.
tips: Start with a shallow squat if you are new to the exercise and gradually increase the depth as you become more comfortable.
Focus on keeping your back straight and your knees aligned with your toes during the squat.
Perform the movement smoothly and with control to maximize muscle activation and coordination.
results.description: Balloon Drill is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Arms.

results.name: Band Squat Row
instructions: Securely loop a resistance band around a sturdy anchor point, at the hip level. Standing with legs at shoulder width, grip the other end of the resistance band palms facing down.
Begin the exercise in a squat position, keeping your chest up and your arms fully extended in front of you.
Stand up explosively, while pulling the band with your arms toward your torso, bringing your elbows to your sides.
Lower your body to a squat position, extending your arms forward. Repeat the movement for the desired amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rounding your lower back or leaning forward during the movement.
Drive through the heels of your feet, focusing on your quads and glutes.
Keep your elbows tucked in when pulling the band near your torso, avoid flaring your elbows.
Exhale during the explosive part of the movement, inhale while slowly returning to the starting position.
results.description: Band Squat Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Hamstrings.
